analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift (new tests at head lines ~1545-1634 for forced Qwen tool_choice) and NativeToolStreamRouterTests.swift (assertion changes about forced-mode framing whitespace). No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache-storage or coordinator code is modified in the supplied evidence.

Behavior these tests pin: with a forced tool_choice (required or named), the stream router drops only ASCII framing whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF) between or around validated Qwen tool calls. Prose after the whitespace, whitespace-only output and non-ASCII whitespace (e.g. NBSP, U+200B) still fail closed with toolChoiceViolation. Tests assert that nothing is emitted (emitted.isEmpty) before a violation. This is conservative and does not weaken validation in the tests themselves.

Threat-model relevance: this touches the provider inference-output handling area (TB-007, T-007 output integrity) only indirectly; a provider operator is already untrusted for output correctness. The test-only changes do not alter T-041 (prefix cache) posture; existing test comments about cacheSalt, kvBackendFallbackReason clamping and heartbeat slots are unchanged context. The fallback-reason clamp test (lines 2398-2412) reaffirms bounded heartbeat fields.

Open question for any production-code pass: the corresponding NativeToolStreamRouter production change (whitespace dropping on legacy, native and MiMo paths) is not in this batch. It should confirm that the dropped whitespace cannot hide content or leak partial output before validation. The second file's excerpt is truncated, so I could not verify its full contents. Neither is a finding, since no production behavior is shown here.
